purpose: Full editor UI concept based on user-selected Compact Workshop style
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-fidelity FULL QUADER LEVEL EDITOR desktop UI mockup in the user's approved COMPACT WORKSHOP style. The result must be a front-on, full-frame landscape application screenshot, approximately 16:9, preferably 2560x1440 detail. Crisp legible small text, plausible native Windows Qt application, no device/monitor, no desk, no outer presentation border, no annotations.

INPUT REFERENCES:
Image 1 is the APPROVED STYLE REFERENCE: Compact Workshop project launcher. Match its dark charcoal surface hierarchy, subtle raised control faces, thin highlight/shadow edges, normal system typography, solid native icons, modest purple accents and clearly bounded integrated sections. This image is the exact visual style authority.
Image 2 is the ACTUAL EDITOR CONTENT/LAYOUT reference. Preserve its real menus, modeling tool rail, Outliner, viewport controls, Inspector/Face Texture/Layers and bottom Asset Browser. Restyle the chrome using Image 1. For this mockup, show a SINGLE LARGE perspective viewport instead of the four-view layout; Quader supports a single view.
Image 3 is SUPPORTING CONTENT: the architectural graybox hallway and populated Inspector. Use it to understand the level scene and transform controls. ABSOLUTELY OMIT all purple numbered circles, fluorescent guide rectangles, callout lines and all black padding outside the application. Those are tutorial annotations, not app UI. Do not reproduce the large bright-purple title bar.

ART DIRECTION:
Extend Compact Workshop faithfully into a full production editor. Mature, substantial, confident desktop-tool character reminiscent of Unreal Engine 4 before UE5. DARK THEME ONLY: near-black viewport surround and content wells, stepped charcoal-gray panel headers and toolbar faces, small raised dark buttons and editable fields, fine one-pixel relief. Clear panel boundaries and strong hierarchy with compact spacing. Almost square controls with 2–4px radii. Body text ordinary clear Segoe-like sans serif, clean and unfussy. Section titles semibold. The user's phrase "rock" means a powerful distinctive professional tool, NEVER music, grunge or theatrics.
Use Quader's purple Q logo and a restrained purple UI selection/focus tint. Preserve semantic red/green/blue axis labels, a thin ORANGE active-viewport border, and warm YELLOW selected-mesh outlines. Purple is not a luminous effect. Subtle dark neutral UI gradients for tangible native controls are appropriate, as in Image 1. No fabric, metal textures, scratches or printed material.

COMPOSITION:
Full screen window with a small dark title bar "Quader — Hallway.qdr", small Q logo, normal Windows window controls.
Top compact menu strip exactly: "File  Edit  View  Select  Create  Object  Mesh  Vertex  Edge  Face  UV  Window  Help".
Below it one compact mode/snapping toolbar with "Object Mode", "Groups", "Grid: 32", "Angle: 15°", "Texture Lock", "Texture Lock Scale". Use the recognizable solid cube and native modeling icons from the editor as appropriate. Avoid giant icon tiles or oversized lettering.
Far-left narrow vertical modeling-tool rail, about 80–95px wide, containing clear small professionally shaded native tool icons and labels "Pivot", "Extrude", "Insert Edge Loop", "Knife", "Cut", "Mirror", "Poly", "Linear Array", "Radial Array", "Path Array", "UV Peel". Keep all readable, tightly composed, no extra tools.
Immediately beside it a roughly 230px-wide Outliner, with a charcoal title strip and recessed near-black tree body. Show a credible small hierarchy for this scene: "Hallway", "Floor", "Walls", "Columns", "Stairs". Use cube/folder glyphs, indentation, disclosure triangles and restrained purple selection on "Walls". No invented feature tabs.
Large central perspective viewport dominates the workspace. Its top scene tab reads "Hallway". A fixed compact control strip above the rendered scene includes select/move/rotate/scale and snapping icons at left and "Environment", "Perspective", "Shaded" at right. Icons are individually readable with clear dark button surfaces.
Show an editable graybox architectural hallway/courtyard viewed from a slightly elevated perspective: a floor, tall L-shaped wall enclosure, repeated rectangular columns and a short stair run. It must look like real simple modeled geometry in a level editor, not a cinematic finished game. Neutral gray surfaces, soft believable lighting, a dark ground grid, and coherent proportions. A section of wall is selected with a thin warm yellow edge outline; a normal red/green/blue transform gizmo is present. Keep line overlays sparse and readable. No large HUD or floating instructions. Scene geometry is central and uncluttered; the UI remains dark even where the geometry is lighter.
On the right, about 310px wide, place the Inspector in a clearly bounded native dock. Show integrated collapsible charcoal headers "General", "Transform", "Export", "Lighting". General: "Name" with value "Walls", "Hidden", "Locked". Transform must preserve STACKED X/Y/Z rows inside distinct Position, Rotation, Scale groups, colored small axis labels separate from numbers. Each numeric entry is visibly editable in a raised graphite field. Example Position X 0.0, Y 0.0, Z 0.0; Rotation X 0.0, Y 0.0, Z 0.0; Scale X 1.0, Y 1.0, Z 1.0. Avoid web-like cards and huge gaps. Export includes "Editor Only"; Lighting includes "Double sided". Put compact "Face Texture" and "Layers" dock headers beneath; keep them collapsed in this particular arrangement to preserve room for useful Inspector fields.
Bottom Asset Browser spans the width beneath the Outliner/viewport/Inspector, with integrated dark header and toolbar: "Asset Browser", "Search assets", "All assets", grid/list view icons. Left is a compact folder tree "Project", "Materials", "Scenes", "Textures". Main asset area has a small, orderly row of native folder/file tiles with labels "Materials", "Scenes", "Textures", "Hallway", "Courtyard", plus a few simple neutral material thumbnails. These are ordinary existing project assets, not a marketplace. Muted yellow folder icons and gray project-file icons with small purple Q marks.
A slim dark bottom status bar reads "1 Mesh Selected" at the right; avoid version text and invented performance statistics.

FUNCTIONAL CONSTRAINTS:
Use only the observed categories/controls described above; don't add a Play button, node editor, timeline, code console, collaboration features or game-engine systems. Do not carry over "New project", "Open project", tutorial or documentation cards from Image 1: it is ONLY the visual style reference. This is the full editor, not the project launcher.
No giant QUADER masthead; typography should fit real editing software. No bright page backgrounds, cream panels, loud accent floods, neon, glow, sci-fi HUD borders, chamfered panels, futuristic fonts, distressed textures, stickers, poster typography, music imagery or overly flat SaaS styling.
Aim for a convincing, cohesive, production-quality mature dark desktop editor whose every panel looks designed by the same team as Compact Workshop.
